## Recruitment as a sequence of survival gates

The literature points to a sequence: spawners produce eggs, environment and transport set larval distribution, prey and production determine age-0 condition, winter filters age-0 fish into age 1, and predation overlap filters age-1 and age-2 fish into age 3.
:::

::: {.stage-strip}
::: {.stage-card .physical}
**Spawners**

SSB, maturity, spawning location
:::

::: {.arrow-card}
&rarr;

Size, diet lipid, total energy
:::

## Alternative Causal Explanations

::: {.alt-grid}
::: {.alt-card}
### A. Bottom-up energy

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Ice["Ice and bloom timing"] --> Prey["Lipid-rich prey"]
  Mix["Summer nutrient flux"] --> Prey
  Prey --> Energy["Age-0 total energy"]
  Energy --> Winter["Winter survival"]
  Winter --> R["Age-3 recruits"]
```

Most diagnostic indicators: age-0 total energy, diet lipid, Calanus/euphausiid biomass.
:::

::: {.alt-card}
### B. Top-down overlap

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Adults["Adult pollock"] --> Overlap["Predator overlap"]
  Arrow["Arrowtooth flounder"] --> Overlap
  Cold["Cold pool"] --> Overlap
  Overlap --> Mort["Age-1/2 mortality"]
  Mort --> R["Age-3 recruits"]
```

Most diagnostic indicators: juvenile-adult overlap, arrowtooth overlap, age-1 predation mortality.
:::

::: {.alt-card}
### C. Transport match-mismatch

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Spawn["Spawning location"] --> Dist["Larval distribution"]
  Wind["Wind and currents"] --> Dist
  Dist --> Match["Prey match"]
  Dist --> Refuge["Predator separation"]
  Match --> R["Age-3 recruits"]
  Refuge --> R
```

Most diagnostic indicators: particle-tracking output, observed spawning distribution, prey/predator collocation.
:::

::: {.alt-card}
### D. Switching control

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  Climate["Climate state"] --> Prey["Bottom-up prey field"]
  Prey --> Age0["Age-0 condition"]
  Prior["Prior cohorts"] --> Pred["Predator field"]
  Age0 --> Overlap["Later overlap"]
  Pred --> Overlap
  Overlap --> R["Age-3 recruits"]
```

Most diagnostic indicators: climate-state interactions, adult biomass, predator biomass, repeated cold/warm year sequences.
:::
:::

## Evidence Weight

::: {.evidence-grid}
::: {.evidence-card}
### Age-0 energy gate

::: {.bar .energy}
:::

Strongest mediator. Fall total energy, lipid-rich prey, and energy density repeatedly link to overwinter survival [@heintz2013; @siddon2013; @sogard2000].
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
### Age-1 predation gate

::: {.bar .pred}
:::

Strong support from adult-juvenile overlap, cannibalism, and arrowtooth predation models [@mueter2006; @spencer2016].
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
### Transport and spawning

::: {.bar .transport}
:::

Moderate support. Spawning-area shifts improve modeled distributions, but transport, temperature, and prey are confounded [@petrik2015].
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
### Simple cold-pool effect

::: {.bar .cold}
:::

Mixed support. Cold pool matters for predator distributions, but a direct cold-pool recruitment mechanism is weak [@mueter2006; @spencer2016].
:::
:::
